text.p: The French franc has a competitive value and there are no reasons to alter intra-European exchange rates, Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said in an interview published in the London Financial Times on Monday.

Reiterating previously-stated views, he said, "Far from being overvalued, the French franc is highly competitive compared with the D-mark and other strong currencies in the ERM and is no longer overvalued against any European currency."
He went on, "The dollar is another matter, but this has absolutely nothing to do with the question of intra-European exchange rates.
"What is clear is that we are a growing economy, not a stagnating one, in the medium term, and the prospects for 1997 in continental Europe and France are quite encouraging."

French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis also supported the present franc-mark exchange rate in an interview published in the French financial daily Les Echos on Monday. He said the parity between the two currencies "must be maintained at its current level".

Trichet said on Friday in a statement that the Bank of France was unshakeably committed to the stability of the franc and dismissed calls from within the Bank for faster rate cuts as purely personal opinions.

"The monetary policy council has only one voice as a collegiate. It is the voice of its president, governor, and spokesman, as is the case for all the other major independent central banks in the world," Trichet said in a statement.

"In Paris, as in Frankfurt, as in Washington, the members of the council speak in a personal capacity. They clearly have the right to do so within the limits of our independent status, given our appreciation of the overriding interest which the law requires of us, that is to defend monetary stability," he said.
Trichet made the written statement in response to a request for comment on a renewed debate in France on the merits of its decade-long policy of keeping the franc stable against the mark.

"The Bank of France is unshakeably committed to the stability of the franc in the group of the most credible European currencies, which comprise in particular the franc, the mark, the guilder, the Belgian franc, the Danish crown and the Austrian schilling," Trichet said.
